en: A serviette; a (usually rectangular) piece of cloth or paper used at the table for wiping the mouth and hands for cleanliness while eating.
A nappy (UK), a diaper (American).

napkin.ety: From Middle English napekyn, napkyn, equivalent to nape (“cloth”) + -kin (diminutive suffix).

ex.en: May I have a napkin, please?
ex.ja: ナプキンを頂けますか。

ex.en: Clean your lips with the napkin.
ex.ja: ナプキンで唇をきれいにしなさい。

ex.en: Could I have a napkin, please?
ex.ja: ナプキンを貰ってもよろしいでしょうか？

note.ja: 古フランス語 nappe（テーブルクロス）+ -kin（小さい）。「小さな布」→「ナプキン」。map と同じ語源。

en: A minor distinction.
Subtlety or fine detail.
To apply a nuance to; to change or redefine in a subtle way.

nuance.ety:
Borrowed from French nuance (“nuance, shade, hue”). Omitting several steps, from Latin nūbēs.
Compare typologically Italian sfumatura (< Latin fūmus).

ex.en: This word has a subtle nuance to it.
ex.ja: その言葉には微妙なニュアンスがある。

ex.en: Mr Jones is very sensitive to the nuances of English and American usage.
ex.ja: ジョーンズ先生は英米の語法の微妙な違いにとても敏感である。

note.ja: フランス語 nuance（色合いの微妙な違い）から。nuer（雲のような陰をつける）、ラテン語 nubes（雲）。

en: A small, compact chunk or clump.
A chicken nugget.
To find nuggets (of something valuable)

nugget.ety: Uncertain, first attested in reference to animals & people in Scotland and in reference to ore chunks in Australia. Possibly from southern English nug (“lump, block”) or Scottish knudge/nudge (“short, sturdy person or animal”) + -et (“forming diminutives”) or from rebracketed alteration of an ingot as a ni(n)got.

ex.en: The miner found a gold nugget.
ex.ja: 鉱夫は金の塊を見つけた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。方言 nug（塊）とされる。「塊」→ 貴重な情報の「断片」。

en: A work of music or set of works with a specified rank in an ordering of a composer's complete published works.
A work, especially of art.

opus.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *h₃épos

English opus
Borrowed from Latin opus.

ex.en: The symphony is his greatest opus.
ex.ja: その交響曲は彼の最高傑作だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 opus（仕事・作品）から。「作品」。operate、opera と同じ語源。magnum opus（代表作）。

en: In an overt manner; publicly; openly.

overtly.ety:
Etymology tree
English overt
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English overtly
From overt + -ly.

ex.en: He never overtly criticized the government.
ex.ja: 彼は公然と政府を批判したことは一度もなかった。

note.ja: overt（公然の）+ -ly。古フランス語 ovrir（開く）の過去分詞。「公然と」。covert の対。

en: Free from pain; without pain or trouble.
Not difficult; easy.

painless.ety: From Middle English paynles, peynlees, equivalent to pain + -less. Compare West Frisian pynleas (“painless”), Dutch pijnloos (“painless”).

ex.en: The treatment is quick and painless.
ex.ja: その治療は短時間で痛みもない。

note.ja: pain（痛み）+ -less。「痛みのない」。

en: Seeming to never end; endlessly; constantly.

perpetually.ety: From Middle English perpetuelly; equivalent to perpetual + -ly.

ex.en: He is perpetually late.
ex.ja: 彼はいつも遅刻している。

note.ja: perpetual（永続的な）+ -ly。per + petere（向かう）。「絶えず」。perpetuate と同じ。

A person who is expecting to give birth.
A dietary supplement to be taken by somebody expecting to give birth.

en: The legal process of verifying the legality of a will.
A copy of a legally recognised and qualified will.
To establish the legality of (a will).

probate.ety: From Middle English probate, from Latin probatus, past participle of probare (“to test, examine, judge of”); see probe, prove.

ex.en: The will is going through probate.
ex.ja: その遺言は検認手続き中だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 probatum（証明されたもの）から。probare。「遺言の検認」。prove と同じ。

en: To acquire or obtain.
To obtain a person as a prostitute for somebody else.

procure.ety: From Middle English procuren, from Old French procurer, from Late Latin prōcūrāre (“to manage, administer”), from prō (“on behalf of”) + cūrō (“to care for”).

ex.en: Where did you procure the information?
ex.ja: どこでその情報を手に入れたのだ。

note.ja: pro（〜のために）+ cur（世話・注意）+ e。気を配って手に入れる →「調達する・入手する」。

en: An inclination, disposition, tendency, preference, or attraction.

propensity.ety: Learned borrowing from New Latin prōpensitās. By surface analysis, propense (“inclined, disposed”) + -ity.

ex.en: He has a propensity to exaggerate.
ex.ja: 彼には大げさに言う癖がある。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ pens（吊るす・傾く）+ ity。前へ傾いていること →「傾向・性癖」。

en: Of, pertaining to, descended from the people or culture of the Punjab, or written in the Punjabi language.
A resident or descendant of or immigrant from the Punjab.
A speaker of the Punjabi language.

Punjabi.ety: Borrowed from Classical Persian پنجابی (panjābī), from پنجاب (panjāb) + ـی (-ī, adjectival suffix). Equivalent to Punjab + -i.

ex.en: We ate Punjabi food at the festival.
ex.ja: 私たちは祭りでパンジャブ料理を食べた。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 panj（5）+ āb（川）。5本の川が流れる「パンジャブ地方」の。

en: The process or an instance of modeling again: applying another model.
Physical modification or redecorating.

ex.en: I spent a lot of money remodeling my house.
ex.ja: リフォームの為にかなりのお金を使っちゃった。

note.ja: re（再び）+ model（型）+ -ing。「作り直すこと」→「改築」。

One who owns or controls property and rents that property to another.

en: To construct a plan of action regarding (something).

ex.en: The company released a roadmap for the next five years.
ex.ja: その会社は今後５年間の工程表を発表した。

note.ja: road + map。「道路地図」→「工程表」。

en: Prayer beads, a string of beads used to keep track of repetitions in prayer, particularly of the Roman Catholic Marian prayer "Hail Mary"…
A Roman Catholic devotion involving the repetition of a series of Marian prayers, usually 5, 15, or 20 decades of "Hail Marys", each deca…

rosary.ety: From Middle English rosarie, from Latin rosārium, here in its sense as a garland of roses. The coin usage referred to the laurel wreath appearing on the obverse bust, as opposed to the bare head on the pollard. Doublet of Rosario and rosarium.

ex.en: She prayed with a rosary.
ex.ja: 彼女はロザリオを手に祈った。

note.ja: ラテン語 rosarium（バラ園）から。祈りを花輪にたとえた →「ロザリオ」。rose と同じ。

en: A rough outline of a topic or situation.
A summary of the horses to be raced on a particular day, with their weights, jockeys, odds, etc.

ex.en: Can you give me a quick rundown of the meeting?
ex.ja: 会議の概要を手短に教えてくれますか。

note.ja: run down（ざっと説明する・荒廃させる）の名詞化。「概要」→ 形容詞で「荒れ果てた」。

en: An action intended to deceive; a trick.
Cunning, guile, trickery.
To deceive or trick using a ruse.

ruse.ety:
From Middle English rūse (“evasive movements of a pursued animal; circuitous course taken by a hunter to pursue a game animal”), from Old French rëuse, ruse (“evasive movements of a pursued animal; trickery”) (modern French ruse (“trick, ruse; cunning, guile”)), from ruser (“to use cunning, to be crafty, beguile”), possibly from Latin rursus (“backward; on the contrary; again, in return”) or Latin recūsāre, from recūsō (“to decline, refuse; to object to, protest, reject”). Doublet of recuse and rouse in the latter case.
The verb is derived from the noun. Compare Middle French ruser (“to use cu

ex.en: All the sweet talk was just a ruse to get her into bed.
ex.ja: 甘い言葉の数々は、ただ彼女をベッドに誘い込むための策略に過ぎなかった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 ruse（獲物が逃げ回ること）から。ruser（追っ手をかわす）。「策略」。

en: A measure of the amount of time a person has been a member of an organization, as compared to other members, and with an eye towards awar…

seniority.ety: From Middle English senyoryte, from Medieval Latin senioritas, from Latin senior (“elder”).

ex.en: In Japan wages are usually in proportion to seniority.
ex.ja: 日本では給料は大体年功序列による。

note.ja: senior + -ity。「年功・先任」。

en: The act of severing or the state of being severed.
A separation.

severance.ety: From sever + -ance, from Middle English severaunce, from Anglo-Norman, Old French sevrance, from sevrer.

ex.en: He received severance pay when he left the company.
ex.ja: 彼は退職時に退職手当を受け取った。

note.ja: sever（切断する）+ -ance。ラテン語 separare（分ける）。「切断」→ 雇用関係を切る「解雇（手当）」。separate と同じ語源。

en: A holster for a sword; a scabbard.
Anything that has a similar shape to a scabbard that is used to hold an object that is longer than it is wide.

sheath.ety:
From Middle English sheth, shethe (“holder for a sword, knife, etc., scabbard, sheath”) [and other forms], from Old English sċēaþ (“sheath”), from Proto-West Germanic *skaiþiju, from Proto-Germanic *skaiþiz (“sheath; covering”), from Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to dissect, split”) (possibly from the notion of a split stick with a sword inserted).
The English word is cognate with Danish skede, Dutch schede, Icelandic skeið, German Scheide, Low German scheed, Norwegian skjede.

ex.en: Eventually, he returned the sword to its sheath.
ex.ja: やがて彼は白刃を鞘に収めた。

note.ja: 古英語 scǣth（さや）から。「さや・覆い」。

en: A rough and rapid method of writing by substituting symbols for letters, words, etc.
Any brief or shortened way of saying or doing something.
To render (spoken or written words) into shorthand.
To use a brief or shortened way of saying or doing something.

shorthand.ety: The noun is derived from short + hand (“handwriting; style of penmanship”). The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: She took down the speech in shorthand.
ex.ja: 彼女はその演説の速記をとった。

ex.en: I have decided to learn shorthand.
ex.ja: 私は速記を習うことに決めた。

ex.en: I've decided to learn shorthand.
ex.ja: 私は速記を習うことに決めた。

note.ja: short + hand（筆跡）。「速記」→「簡略な言い方」。

en: Placed on a short list.

ex.en: Her novel was shortlisted for the prize.
ex.ja: 彼女の小説はその賞の最終候補に残った。

note.ja: shortlist（最終候補名簿に載せる）+ -ed。short + list。

en: The state of being singular, distinct, peculiar, uncommon or unusual.
An unusual action or behaviour.

singularity.ety: From Middle English singularite, from Old French singularité, from Late Latin singulāritās (“singleness”), from Latin singulāris (“single”). By surface analysis, singular + -ity.

ex.en: Some scientists talk about a technological singularity.
ex.ja: 技術的特異点について語る科学者もいる。

note.ja: singular（特異な）+ -ity。「特異性」→ 数学・物理の「特異点」。single と同じ。

en: A humanoid figure made with large snowballs stacked on each other. Human traits like a face and arms may be fashioned with sticks (arms),…
A score of eight, especially within one inning (in baseball) or on one hole (in golf, where it is also known as dogballs).

snowman.ety:
* snow + -man.
* (score of eight; card ranked eight): A typical snowman, built from two balls of snow, resembles a figure eight.

ex.en: It's fun to build a snowman in winter.
ex.ja: 冬に雪だるまを作るのは楽しい。

ex.en: Tom and Mary are outside building a snowman.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは外で雪だるまを作っている。

ex.en: Tom and Mary are outside making a snowman.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは外で雪だるまを作っている。

note.ja: snow（雪）+ man。「雪だるま」。

To instruct (somebody), usually subconsciously and mostly by example, in the etiquette of a society.

en: In the shape of a square; at right angles.
Firmly and solidly.

squarely.ety: From square + -ly. First use appears c. 1557 in the writings of Robert Recorde.

ex.en: The ball hit him squarely in the face.
ex.ja: ボールが彼の顔にまともに当たった。

note.ja: square（四角い・まっすぐな）+ -ly。「まともに・真正面から」。

en: A person or thing likened to a stereotypical stepmother, having cold, cruel, or ungenerous qualities.
An animal, typically a bird, who raises the offspring of another animal.

stepmother.ety: From Middle English stepmoder, from Old English stēopmōdor, from Proto-Germanic *steupamōdēr (“stepmother”), corresponding to step- + mother. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Stäifmuur (“stepmother”), Dutch stiefmoeder (“stepmother”), German Low German Steevmoder (“stepmother”), German Stiefmutter (“stepmother”), Danish stedmor (“stepmother”), Swedish styvmor (“stepmother”), Icelandic stjúpmóðir (“stepmother”). Compare also West Frisian styfmem (“stepmother”).

ex.en: The stepmother was hard on her.
ex.ja: 継母は彼女に辛く当たった。

ex.en: This part of the land belongs to my stepmother.
ex.ja: この地所は私の継母のものです。

ex.en: This is my stepmother.
ex.ja: こちらは、継母です。

note.ja: 古英語 stēop（孤児の）+ mother。「親を亡くした子の母」→「継母」。stepfather と同じ。

en: Of a peacock or other fowl: to stand or walk stiffly, with the tail erect and spread out.
To walk haughtily or proudly with one's head held high.
A step or walk done stiffly and with the head held high, often due to haughtiness or pride; affected dignity in walking.
An instrument for adjusting the pleats of a ruff.

strut.ety:

The English word is cognate with Danish strutte (“to bulge, bristle”), Low German str

ex.en: The rooster strutted around the yard.
ex.ja: おんどりが庭を気取って歩き回った。

note.ja: 古英語 strūtian（突っ張る）から。「気取って歩く」→ 突っ張る「支柱」。

To give up, or give in.

ex.ja: 彼は権力に屈した。

ex.en: Don't succumb to pressure!
ex.ja: プレッシャーに負けるな。

en: To behave (especially to walk or carry oneself) in a pompous, superior manner.
To boast or brag noisily; to bluster; to bully.
Confidence, pride.
A bold or arrogant strut.

swagger.ety: A frequentative form of swag (“to sway”), first attested in A Midsummer Night's Dream (1595), see quotations.

ex.en: The speaker swaggered into the lecture hall.
ex.ja: 演説者はふんぞり返って講堂に入っていった。

note.ja: swag（揺れる）+ -er。シェイクスピアが使った語。「いばって歩く」。

en: To twist or whirl, as an eddy.
To be arranged in a twist, spiral or whorl.
A whirling eddy.
A twist or coil of something.

swirl.ety: From Middle English swirlen (“to eddy, swirl”), probably from Old Norse *svirla (“to swirl”), a frequentative form of Old Norse sverra (“to swing, twirl”). Cognate with Scots swirl, sworl (“to eddy, swirl”), Norwegian Nynorsk svirla (“to whirl around; swirl”), Swedish sorla (“to murmur, buzz”), Dutch zwirrelen (“to swirl”). Compare also West Frisian swiere (“to reel, whirl”), Dutch zwieren (“to reel, swing around”), German Low German swirren (“to whizz, whirl or buzz around”), German schwirren (“to whirr, whizz, buzz”), Swedish svirra (“to whirr about, buzz, hum”), Danish svirre (“to whizz, wh

ex.en: Leaves swirled in the wind.
ex.ja: 木の葉が風に舞って渦を巻いた。

note.ja: 中英語 swyrl（渦）から。北欧語に由来するとされる。「渦を巻く」。

The measure of an angle.

note.ja: ギリシャ文字 θ。フェニキア文字に由来する。

en: Exceptional in some degree.
Exceptionally. Very.
A dull, heavy sound.
A beating.

ex.en: They had been thumping the drum all along.

note.ja: thump（ドンとたたく）+ -ing。擬音的な語。「どきどきする」→（英口語）「大きな」。

en: Having undergone transcription.
Prerecorded for later broadcasting.

ex.en: The interview was recorded and transcribed.

note.ja: transcribe（書き写す）+ -ed。trans + scribere（書く）。transcript と同じ scrib。

ex.en: The last tsar of Russia was Nicholas II.
ex.ja: ロシア最後の皇帝はニコライ２世だった。

en: A wealthy and powerful business person.
A business simulator game, typically involving building and managing some form of business or infrastructure.

tycoon.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 大君 (“great lord, prince”), a title for the shōgun. Related to taipan, from Cantonese 大班 (daai⁶ baan¹). The game sense was derived from the use of tycoon in titles of games in which one plays a tycoon (e.g., RollerCoaster Tycoon).

ex.en: The tycoon endowed each son with a million dollars.
ex.ja: あの大事業家は息子それぞれに１００万ドルを残した。

ex.en: He was a stock-market tycoon until the bears got him.
ex.ja: 株でやられるまで彼は証券市場の帝王でしたよ。

en: Tumultuous, noisy excitement.
Loud, confused noise, especially when coming from several sources.
To throw into uproar or confusion.
To make an uproar.

en: Alert watchfulness.
Close and continuous attention.

vigilance.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vigilance, from Latin vigilantia.

ex.ja: 人生での成功の道は勤勉さと用心深さにある。

note.ja: vigilant（用心深い）+ -ance。ラテン語 vigil（目を覚ましている）。「警戒」。vigil（徹夜）と同じ。

en: A member of the peerage, above a baron but below a count or earl.
Any of various nymphalid butterflies of the genus Tanaecia. Other butterflies in this genus are called earls and counts.

viscount.ety: From Anglo-Norman viscounte, from Medieval Latin vicecomes, from Latin vice + comes. Equivalent to vice- + count. Doublet of vicecomes and vicomte.

ex.en: The viscount lived in a large country house.
ex.ja: その子爵は田舎の大きな屋敷に住んでいた。

en: A native or inhabitant of the West, of the Western world—The United States, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. (Also wri…
A native or inhabitant of the Wild West. (Also written capitalized as Westerner.)

ex.en: Generally speaking, Westerners don't eat fish raw.
ex.ja: 一般的に言えば、西欧人は魚を生では食べない。

ex.en: Some Westerners may think our houses are lacking in everything they consider essential.
ex.ja: 西洋人の中には、私たちの家屋には彼らが不可欠と考えるもの全てが欠けていると思う人もいるだろう。

note.ja: western（西の）+ -er。「西洋人」。

The building or structure containing such machinery.
To rotate with a sweeping motion.
To (become disengaged and) rotate freely.

ex.ja: 新しいソフトウェアで作業の流れが改善した。

note.ja: work（仕事）+ flow（流れ）。「作業の流れ」。

en: Something that is wrapped around something else as a cover or protection: a wrapping.
An outer garment; a loose robe or dressing gown.

wrapper.ety: From Middle English wrappere, equivalent to wrap + -er.

ex.en: He took full advantage of the wrapper.
ex.ja: 彼は風呂敷を十分に活用した。

ex.en: Don't eat the wrapper.
ex.ja: 包み紙は食べちゃダメよ。

ex.en: I slowly opened the candy wrapper, quietly so that I wouldn't wake my parents.
ex.ja: 父さんと母さんが目を覚まさないように、音を立てず、そぉ〜っとキャンディの包みを開けました。

note.ja: wrap（包む）+ -er。「包むもの」→「包み紙」。

en: A devotee or adherent of yoga.
To turn (someone) into a yogi; to lead into practicing yoga.

yogi.ety: From Hindi योगी (yogī), from Sanskrit योगिन् (yogin), from the verbal root yuj (class 7 present युनक्ति (yunakti, “to connect”)), from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm.

ex.en: The yogi sat quietly in meditation.
ex.ja: ヨガ行者は静かに瞑想していた。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 yogin から。yoga（結びつけること）。「ヨガ行者」。yoke と同じ印欧祖語。

en: The name of the Latin script letter Z/z.
Something Z-shaped. Found in compounds.
To sleep or nap. (Compare zzz, catch some z's.)

zee.ety: Likely an alteration of zed (which see for more), by analogy with other letters such as bee, dee, tee and vee. ex.en: Americans say "zee" for the letter Z.
ex.ja: アメリカ人は Z の文字を「ズィー」と読む。

en: The power to attract, entice; the quality causing attraction.
To entice; to attract.

allure.ety: From Middle English aluren, from Old French aleurer, alurer, from a (“to, towards”) (Latin ad) + leurre (“lure”). By surface analysis, al- + lure.

ex.ja: 彼女の魅力に彼は心を奪われた。

ex.ja: 彼はついに彼女の財産に釣られて結婚した。

en: An acute infectious disease of herbivores, especially sheep and cattle, caused by Bacillus anthracis.
The human disease that can occur in humans through contact with infected herbivores, tissue from infected animals, or high concentrations…

ex.en: Anthrax is a serious disease.
ex.ja: 炭疽は深刻な病気だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 anthrax（石炭・できもの）から。皮膚に黒いかさぶたができることから「炭疽」。

en: Of or relating to water.
Consisting mostly of water. Often used in the expression "aqueous solution".

aqueous.ety: Formed from Latin aqua + -ous (or from Medieval Latin aqueus), partly the analogy of Middle French aqueux (itself actually from Latin aquosus). Or based on the analogy of Latin terreus from terra.

ex.en: The chemical is dissolved in an aqueous solution.
ex.ja: その化学物質は水溶液に溶かされている。

note.ja: ラテン語 aqua（水）から。「水の・水溶性の」。aquarium と同じ。

That which is attained, or obtained by exertion.

attainment.ety: From attain + -ment; compare Old French ataignement.

ex.ja: その学校は学業成績の向上に力を入れている。

note.ja: attain（達成する）+ -ment。ad + tangere（触れる）。「手が届くこと」→「達成」。tangible と同じ。

A starship of comparable role.

battleship.ety: From battle + ship; shortened from line-of-battle ship, attested 1794.

ex.ja: その古い戦艦は今では博物館になっている。

note.ja: フランスのバイヨンヌ（Bayonne）で作られた短剣から。「銃剣」。

en: Any grenade, mortar shell, or artillery shell (hollow metal object) containing a charge that can explode.
Something that is very surprising, shocking, amazing or sensational.

bombshell.ety: From bomb + shell. The dating show sense was popularized by the series Love Island in 2015.

ex.ja: いきなり爆弾発言ぶっこんできた。

ex.ja: いきなり爆弾発言ぶっこんできた。

en: An inhabitant of Great Britain, particularly (historical) a Celt from the area of Roman Britain or (obsolete) a Welshman; a British person.
A citizen of the United Kingdom or (historical, obsolete) its overseas empire.

Briton.ety:

From Old French Breton, from Latin Brittō. Doublet of Breton and Brython.

ex.en: The Romans tried to civilize the ancient Britons.
ex.ja: ローマ人は古代ブリトン人の文明化を試みた。

note.ja: ラテン語 Brito（ブリトン人）から。古代ブリテン島のケルト系住民 →「英国人」。Britain と同じ。

en: The experience of long-term exhaustion and diminished interest, especially in one's career.
A person who has the experience of long-term exhaustion and diminished interest.

ex.en: Long hours can lead to burnout.
ex.ja: 長時間労働は燃え尽き症候群につながることがある。

note.ja: burn out（燃え尽きる）の名詞化。「燃え尽き症候群」。

en: Each of the two large fleshy halves of the posterior part of the body between the base of the back, the perineum, and the top of the legs.
The convexity of a ship behind, under the stern.

buttock.ety: Inherited from Middle English buttok, probably from Old English buttuc (“end; end piece”; also, “short piece of land”). Attested with its current anatomical meaning since 1300. A diminutive form of what is presumably the Old English precursor of butt + -ock (diminutive suffix).

ex.en: He got a shot in the buttock.
ex.ja: 彼はお尻に注射を打たれた。

note.ja: butt（端・尻）+ -ock（小さい）。「尻」。

en: The acquisition of a controlling interest in a business or corporation by outright purchase or by purchase of a majority of issued shares…
The use of grant monies to pay for another person to perform the usual duties, especially teaching duties, of someone engaged on the fund…

ex.en: Auctions are annoying, so I bought it instantly with a buyout.
ex.ja: オクは面倒なので即決で一回買っただけ。

note.ja: buy out（買い取る）の名詞化。「買収」。

en: Relating to or affected with cancer.
Growing or spreading rapidly to the point of harm.

cancerous.ety: From Middle English cancerous, from Latin cancerōsus, from cancer (“crab; tumor, cancer”) + -ōsus (adjective-forming suffix). By surface analysis, cancer + -ous.

ex.en: The doctor removed a cancerous tumor.
ex.ja: 医師はがん性の腫瘍を取り除いた。

note.ja: cancer + -ous。「がんの」。

en: A metric unit of mass equal to exactly 200 mg, chiefly used for measuring precious stones and pearls.
Any of several small units of mass used for measuring precious stones and pearls, equivalent to 189–212 mg.

carat.ety: From Middle French carat, from Italian carato, from Arabic قِيرَاط (qīrāṭ, “carat, similarly small units such as inches”), from Ancient Greek κεράτιον (kerátion, “hornlet, carob seed”), from κέρας (kéras, “horn”) + -ιον (-ion, diminutive suffix). Doublet of quilate and keratin.

ex.en: She wears a two-carat diamond ring.
ex.ja: 彼女は２カラットのダイヤの指輪をしている。

note.ja: アラビア語 qīrāṭ から。ギリシャ語 keration（イナゴマメの種）。種を重さの単位にしたことから。

en: An invasive malignant tumour derived from epithelial tissue that tends to metastasize to other areas of the body.

carcinoma.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin carcinōma (“tumour; ulcer; carcinoma”), from Ancient Greek κᾰρκῐ́νωμᾰ (kărkĭ́nōmă, “sore, ulcer; cancer”), from καρκινόω (karkinóō, “to make (something) resemble a crab”, in the mediopassive "to become cancerous; to suffer from cancer") + -μᾰ (-mă, action noun suffix). Καρκινόω is derived from καρκῐ́νος (karkĭ́nos, “crab; the zodiac sign Cancer; sore, ulcer; cancer”) (according to Paul of Aegina (c. 625 – c. 690) in his Medical Compendium in Seven Books, because the veins surrounding a cancerous tumour resemble a crab’s legs). The English word is a doublet of cance

ex.en: He was diagnosed with a skin carcinoma.
ex.ja: 彼は皮膚がんと診断された。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 karkinōma（がん）から。karkinos（カニ）。cancer（カニ座）と同じ発想。

en: A warning.
A qualification or exemption.
To qualify a statement with a caveat or proviso.
To formally object to something.

caveat.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin caveat (“may he/she/it beware”), third-person singular present active subjunctive of caveō (“to beware of”). Doublet of show, both ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to heed, look, feel, take note of”).

ex.en: There is one caveat: the offer ends today.
ex.ja: 一つ注意点がある。その特典は今日で終わりだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 caveat（用心させよ）から。cavere（用心する）。caveat emptor（買い手は用心せよ）。「但し書き」。caution と同系。

en: Roe of the sturgeon or of certain other large fish, considered a delicacy.
A food preparation made through the spherification of a flavorful liquid, resulting in small roe-like balls similar in texture and appear…

caviar.ety: Borrowed from Middle French caviar, from Venetan caviaro (earlier found as Italian caviale), probably by way of Ottoman Turkish خاویار (havyar), from Classical Persian خَاوْیَار (xāwyār). Doublet of ajvar.

ex.en: Steak and caviar are my favorite foods.
ex.ja: ステーキとキャビアが私の好物だ。

ex.en: He hasn't actually eaten caviar.
ex.ja: 彼はキャビアを実際に食べたことがない。

ex.en: Steak and caviar are my favorite dishes.
ex.ja: ステーキとキャビアが私の好物だ。

note.ja: トルコ語 havyar から。ペルシャ語 khāviyār（卵を持つ）とされる。

en: A small, exclusive group of individuals, usually having some common characteristic such as lifestyle or social status, or common purpose;…
A subgraph isomorphic to a complete graph.
To form a clique (“small, exclusive group of individuals, usually having some common characteristic”; noun sense 1); to associate with ot…
To act with others secretly to gain a desired end; to plot, to scheme.

clique.ety:
The noun is borrowed from French clique (“exclusive group of individuals; (archaic or obsolete) group of people hired to applaud or boo, claque”), from cliquer (“to clap; to clack, to click”), ultimately of imitative origin.
The proper noun and verb are derived from the noun.

ex.en: I'm opposed to political power being monopolized within a clique.
ex.ja: 政権のたらい回しは反対だ。

note.ja: フランス語 clique（徒党）から。cliquer（カチッと鳴る）とされる。「派閥」。claque と同系。

en: The act of contemplating; being highly concentrated in thought; musing.
Holy meditation.

contemplation.ety: From Middle English contemplacioun, from Old French contemplation, from Latin contemplatio. By surface analysis, contemplate + -ion.

ex.en: He sat by the lake in quiet contemplation.
ex.ja: 彼は湖のほとりに座って静かに思いにふけった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ templ（神殿・観察の場）+ ation。じっと見つめること →「熟考・瞑想」。

en: Created in a deliberate, rather than natural or spontaneous, way.
Unnatural, forced; artificial, or unrealistic.

ex.en: They contrived to arrive in time after all.
ex.ja: 彼らはどうやらなんとか遅れずに到着できた。

ex.en: He contrived a new engine that does not use gas.
ex.ja: 彼はガソリンを使わないエンジンを考案した。

ex.en: I contrived to leave my wallet behind.
ex.ja: 私は財布を忘れてくるというへまをしでかしてしまった。

note.ja: contrive（工夫する）+ -ed。「工夫された」→「わざとらしい」。

en: The outermost-but-one whorl of a flower, composed of petals, when it is not the same in appearance as the outermost whorl (the calyx); it…

corolla.ety: From Latin corōlla (“small garland, chaplet or wreath”), diminutive of corōna (“garland, chaplet, wreath”).

ex.en: The flower has a bright yellow corolla.
ex.ja: その花は明るい黄色の花冠を持っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 corolla（小さな冠）から。corona（冠）。「花冠」。crown と同じ。トヨタの車名もここから。

en: Marked with parallel folds, ridges or furrows.
Bent into regular curved folds or grooves.

ex.en: The box is made of corrugated cardboard.
ex.ja: その箱は段ボールでできている。

note.ja: corrugate（波形にする）+ -ed。ラテン語 ruga（しわ）。corrugated cardboard（段ボール）。

en: Not in good working condition; defective, faulty.
Grouchy, grumpy, irritable; easily upset.

cranky.ety: From crank + -y. Compare Middle Low German krankich (“sickly, unwell”).

ex.en: He was so cranky last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜彼は怒りっぽかったな。

ex.en: Tom is a cranky old man.
ex.ja: トムは風変わりな老人だ。

ex.en: It is easy to get the cranky man's goat by teasing him.
ex.ja: 気難しい人は、からかうとすぐ腹を立てる。

note.ja: crank（変わり者）+ -y。「気難しい・不機嫌な」。

Buxom or curvaceous.

From curve + -y.

ex.ja: その道はカーブが多い。

note.ja: curve + -y。「曲線の多い」。

en: Being affected by delusions.

ex.en: He is deluded if he thinks he can win easily.
ex.ja: 簡単に勝てると思っているなら、彼は思い違いをしている。

note.ja: delude（欺く）+ -ed。de + ludere（遊ぶ・からかう）。「思い違いをした」。illusion と同じ lud。

en: To make worse; to make inferior in quality or value; to impair.
To grow worse; to be impaired in quality; to degenerate.

deteriorate.ety: Learned borrowing from Late Latin dēteriorātus, perfect passive participle of Late Latin dēteriorō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), further from Latin dēterior (“worse”). Cognate with French détériorer.

ex.en: It seems to me that the weather will deteriorate.
ex.ja: 天気が崩れそうだね。

ex.en: It seems the weather will deteriorate.
ex.ja: 天気が崩れそうだね。

ex.en: Frequently clear and balmy weather deteriorates and it soon rains cats and dogs.
ex.ja: 晴れた、さわやかな天気がくずれたと思うと、土砂降りになることがよくある。

note.ja: ラテン語 deterior（より悪い）から。「悪化する」。

en: To break up or (cause to) cease to exist; to disperse.

disband.ety: Attested since the 1590s, from Middle French desbander (Modern French débander), from des- (English dis-) + bande (English band), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to tie”). By surface analysis, dis- + band.

ex.en: I hear that popular group will be disbanded.
ex.ja: あの人気グループが解散するそうだ。

note.ja: dis（離す）+ band（集団）。「集団をばらばらにする」→「解散する」。

en: Not in order; marked by disorder or disarray.
Not acting in an orderly way, as the functions of the body or mind.
A person who acts in a disorderly manner.
In a confused or lawless manner.

disorderly.ety: From disorder + -ly (adjectival suffix) or from dis- + orderly.

ex.en: He was arrested for disorderly conduct.
ex.ja: 彼は治安を乱した罪で逮捕された。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ order（秩序）+ -ly。「無秩序な」。

en: Deeply hurt, saddened, or worried; incapacitated by distress.
Mad; insane.

distraught.ety: From Middle English distraught, blend of distract (“distracted”) and straught (“stretched, distraught”), past participle of strecchen (“to stretch”). Compare also bestraught, extraught, forstraught, etc. More at distract, stretch.

ex.en: I was distraught over what to do because everything was going poorly.
ex.ja: 何もかもうまくいかず、どうしていいか迷って苦悶した。

note.ja: distract の古い過去分詞形。「取り乱した」。

en: To rain lightly.
To shed slowly in minute drops or particles.
Light rain.
Very small, numerous, and uniformly dispersed water drops, mist, or sprinkle. Unlike fog droplets, drizzle falls to the ground.

drizzle.ety: Perhaps a back-formation from dryseling, a dissimilated variant of Middle English drysning (“a falling of dew”), from Northumbrian Old English drysnan (“to extinguish”), related to Old English drēosan (“to fall, to decline”), making it cognate to modern English droze and drowse. Compare also dialectal Swedish drösla.

ex.en: It began to drizzle.
ex.ja: 小雨が降り始めました。

note.ja: 中英語 dresen（落ちる）とされる。「霧雨」→（ソースなどを）少量たらす。

ex.ja: 彼らは村を洪水から守るために堤防を補強した。

en: Emerging; coming into view or into existence; nascent; new.
Arising unexpectedly, especially if also calling for immediate reaction.
A plant whose root system grows underwater, but whose shoot, leaves and flowers grow up and above the water.

emergent.ety: From Latin ēmergēns, present participle of ēmergō. The medical sense is a back-formation from emergency.

ex.en: The country is an emergent economic power.
ex.ja: その国は新興の経済大国だ。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ merg（浸る）+ ent。水中から現れつつある →「新興の・現れ出る」。emergency（緊急事態）と同じ。

en: Having the ability to enchant; charming, delightful.
An act of enchantment.

ex.en: The village is enchanting in spring.
ex.ja: その村は春になると魅惑的だ。

note.ja: enchant（魅了する）+ -ing。ラテン語 incantare（呪文をかける）、in + cantare（歌う）。chant と同じ。

en: To lure; to attract by arousing desire or hope.

entice.ety: From Middle English enticen, from Old French enticier (“to stir up or excite”), from a Vulgar Latin *intitiāre (“I set on fire”), from in- + titiō (“firebrand (tool)”), from Proto-Italic *tītjō (“heating”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *teih₁- (“to become hot, melt or to end”).

ex.en: In the end, entice someone with food to win.
ex.ja: 結局、胃袋を掴んだもの勝ちだよね。

ex.en: She enticed him into escaping from prison.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼をそそのかして刑務所から脱走させた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 enticier（あおる）から。ラテン語 titio（燃えさし）とされる。「火をつける」→「誘い込む」。

en: Praised, honored.
Noble, sublime; heavenly.

ex.en: The medieval church despised the body and exalted the spirit.
ex.ja: 中世の教会は肉体をさげすみ霊をたたえた。

note.ja: exalt（高める）+ -ed。ex + altus（高い）。「高位の・高揚した」。altitude と同じ。

en: A young female horse.

filly.ety: From Old Norse fylja (whence Danish føl), related to foal. Cognate with Dutch veulen, German Fohlen.

ex.en: The filly won her first race.
ex.ja: その雌の子馬は初めてのレースで勝った。

note.ja: 古北欧語 fylja（雌の子馬）から。foal と同系。

en: The state of being formal.
Something said or done as a matter of form.

formality.ety: From Middle French formalité. equivalent to formal + -ity.

ex.en: Let's do away with all formalities.
ex.ja: 堅苦しい礼儀は一切抜きにしましょう。

ex.en: Let's skip the formalities now, it's time to eat.
ex.ja: 堅苦しい挨拶は抜きにして、さあ食べましょう。

ex.en: In general, young people dislike formality.
ex.ja: 一般に若者は形式を嫌う。

note.ja: formal（形式的な）+ -ity。「形式的手続き」。

en: Mental or emotional strength that enables courage in the face of adversity.

fortitude.ety: From Middle English fortitude, from Old French, from Latin fortitūdō (“bravery, strength”), from fortis (“brave, strong”).

ex.en: She faced her illness with great fortitude.
ex.ja: 彼女は不屈の精神で病気に立ち向かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 fortitudo（強さ）から。fortis（強い）。「不屈の精神」。fort、force と同じ。

One who takes significant risks.

ex.ja: メアリーに会う以前、トムはプロのギャンブラーだった。

ex.ja: 多くのギャンブラーは競馬でお金を儲けもし、失いもする。

note.ja: gamble（賭ける）+ -er。game と同系。「ギャンブラー」。

en: A short snorting sound, often to show disapproval, or used as a reply when one is reluctant to speak.
The snorting cry of a pig.
To make a grunt or grunts.
To make a grunt or grunts.

grunt.ety:
From Middle English grunten, from Old English grunnettan (“to grunt”), from Proto-West Germanic *grunnattjan, from Proto-Germanic *grunnatjaną (“to grunt”), frequentative of Proto-Germanic *grunnōną (“to grunt”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrun- (“to shout”).
Cognate with German grunzen (“to grunt”), Danish grynte (“to grunt”). The noun senses are all instances of zero derivation from the verb.

ex.en: The pig gave a loud grunt as it ate.
ex.ja: 豚は食べながら大きな声でぶうぶう鳴いた。

note.ja: 古英語 grunnettan（ぶうぶう言う）から。擬音語。「うなる」→ 下っ端の兵士。

en: A strong, abrupt rush of wind.
Any rush or outburst (of water, emotion, etc.).
To blow in gusts.

gust.ety:
Apparently from an unrecorded Middle English *gust, from Old Norse gustr (“a gust, blast”), from Proto-Germanic *gustiz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰew-. Cognate with Icelandic gustur (“gust of wind”). Related also to Old Norse gusa (“to gush forth”), Old High German gussa (“flood”), Middle English guschen (> English gush).
The English word was not recorded before Shakespeare.

ex.en: The gust of wind rose suddenly.
ex.ja: 突然に一陣の風が起こった。

ex.en: The wind blew in gusts.
ex.ja: 強風が断続的に吹いた。

ex.en: A gust of wind swelled the sails.
ex.ja: 一陣の風をうけて帆がふくらんだ。

note.ja: 古北欧語 gustr（突風）から。「突風」。

en: Allowable, according to Muslim religious customs, to have or do.
Fit to eat according to Muslim religious customs.
In a halal manner; in accordance with Muslim religious customs.
To make halal.
to allow

ex.en: I only eat halal meat.
ex.ja: ハラルのお肉しか食べないよ。

note.ja: アラビア語 ḥalāl（許された）から。イスラム法で許されたもの。

en: Showing accord in feeling or action.
Having components pleasingly or appropriately combined.

harmonious.ety: From Middle French harmonieux; by surface analysis, harmony + -ous.

ex.en: Tom and Mary live a harmonious life together.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは仲睦まじく暮らしている。

ex.en: The villa was harmonious with the scenery.
ex.ja: その別荘は風景と調和していた。

note.ja: harmony（調和）+ -ous。ギリシャ語 harmonia（結合）。「調和のとれた」。

hashtag.ety: From earlier hash tag, from hash (sign) + tag. The hash sign # was initially proposed as tag hash by Chris Messina to create groups on Twitter, modeled after the IRC channel prefix. First published use as hash tag by Stowe Boyd in 2007.

ex.en: Use this hashtag when you post photos.
ex.ja: 写真を投稿するときはこのハッシュタグを使ってください。

note.ja: hash（#記号）+ tag（札）。2007年ごろに広まった造語。

en: A traditional headscarf worn by Muslim women, covering the hair and neck.
The practice, among Muslim women, of covering the body after the age of puberty in front of non-related (non-family) adult males.

ex.en: I want to try and wear a hijab.
ex.ja: ヒジャブ、被ってみたい。

ex.en: Your hijab is a lovely color.
ex.ja: あなたのヒジャブ、素敵な色ね。

ex.en: I want to try a hijab.
ex.ja: ヒジャブ、してみたい。

note.ja: アラビア語 ḥijāb（覆い）から。イスラム教徒の女性のスカーフ。

zh: 到目前為止 /到目前为止

en: Up to this or that time.

hitherto.ety:
The adverb is derived from Middle English hiderto (“to the present time, until now; up to this point”), from hider (“in this direction, to or toward this place; up to the present time, until now”) (from Old English hider (“to here, hither”)) + to (“in the direction of, toward; etc.”). By surface analysis, hither + to.
The adjective is derived from the adverb.

ex.en: The history of all hitherto existing societies is the history of class struggles.
ex.ja: 昔から今に至るまで存在する、あらゆる社会の歴史は階級闘争の歴史である。

note.ja: hither（ここへ）+ to（まで）。「これまで」。

en: Of or relating to hyperbole.
Using hyperbole: exaggerated.

hyperbolic.ety: From Latin hyperbolic(us), from Ancient Greek ὑπερβολικός (huperbolikós). First attested in the 15th century. By surface analysis, hyperbol(e) + -ic.

ex.en: His hyperbolic claims were hard to believe.
ex.ja: 彼の誇張した主張は信じがたかった。

note.ja: hyperbole（誇張法）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 hyper（越えて）+ ballein（投げる）。「投げすぎる」→「誇張した」。数学では「双曲線の」。

en: Removed from office in accordance with Article II, Section 4 of the United States Constitution.

ex.en: I impeached his motives.
ex.ja: 私は彼の動機を疑った。

note.ja: impeach（弾劾する）+ -ed。古フランス語 empechier（妨げる）、ラテン語 pedica（足かせ）。

en: The act of impeding; that which impedes; a hindrance.
A measure of the opposition to the flow of an alternating current in a circuit; the aggregation of its resistance, and inductive and capa…

impedance.ety: From impede + -ance. In sense 2 and sense 3 it was coined by English mathematician and physicist Oliver Heaviside in 1886.

ex.en: The speaker has an impedance of eight ohms.
ex.ja: そのスピーカーのインピーダンスは８オームだ。

note.ja: impede（妨げる）+ -ance。ラテン語 impedire（足かせをはめる）、in + pes（足）。電気の流れを妨げる量。

A slope.
A portal of a subway tunnel.

en: Sitting on eggs for the purpose of hatching young; a brooding on, or keeping warm, to develop the life within, by any process.
The development of a disease from its causes, or the period of such development.

incubation.ety: From Latin incubātiō, from incubō (“to lie on”).

ex.en: The incubation period of the virus is about a week.
ex.ja: そのウイルスの潜伏期間は約１週間だ。

en: A patch or other object that indicates a person's official or military rank, or membership in a group or organization.
A symbol or token of personal power, status, or office, or of an official body of government or jurisdiction.

isotope.ety: From iso- (“equal”) + -tope (“place”), because the different isotopes of an element always occupy the same place in the periodic table. The term was coined by Scottish doctor Margaret Todd in 1909 and first used publicly on February 27, 1913 by English chemist Frederick Soddy.

ex.ja: 炭素にはいくつかの同位体がある。

en: A power saw with fine teeth and a narrow blade which can cut curves in wood or metal.
A jigsaw puzzle.
To cut something using a jigsaw.

ex.ja: ジグソーとは糸鋸の事で、名前の由来はそこからきているの。

One of a number of coniferous trees which resemble junipers.

juniper.ety: From Late Middle English junyper, juniperus, from Latin iūniperus (“juniper-tree”).

ex.en: Gin is flavored with juniper berries.
ex.ja: ジンはネズの実で香りづけされている。

note.ja: ラテン語 juniperus から。ジンの香りづけに使う。gin（ジン）はオランダ語 genever（ネズ）の短縮。

ja: 同類の（kindred spirit：気の合う人）

en: Distant and close relatives, collectively; kin.
People of the same ethnic descent, not including speaker; brethren.
Of the same nature, or of similar character.
Connected, related, cognate, akin.

kindred.ety: From Middle English kyndrede, from older kynrede (“kindred”), from Old English *cynrēd, *cynrǣden (“kindred, family, stock”), from cynn (“kind, kin, lineage”) + -rǣden (“condition, state”). Equivalent to kin + -red, see these. The -d- is epenthetic between a nasal and a liquid (as e.g. in spindle).

ex.en: I found a kindred spirit in Bob.
ex.ja: ボブとはすっかり意気投合した。

ex.en: Trade knows neither friends or kindred.
ex.ja: 親子の中でも金銭は他人。

ex.en: He and I are kindred spirits.
ex.ja: 私と彼とはすっかり意気投合している。

note.ja: 古英語 cynn（一族）+ ræden（状態）。kin と同じ。「同類の」→ kindred spirit（気の合う人）。

en: An item of confectionery consisting of a piece of candy or sweet attached to a stick.
Something having the shape of a lollipop: a linear stem connected to a round body.
To prune the lower branches of a tree or other plant so that new growth appears only at the top, where more light is received.

lollipop.ety:
By surface analysis, loll (“laze, hang loose”) + y + pop (“shot, try, burst, enter”); likely through lolly (“head, tongue”). Attested from 1784. Compare lollygag and lollypoop.
An unlikely derivation is from Romani loli (“red”) + phabaj (“apple”); candy apples are often red and placed on a stick to keep the person's hands dry, similar to lollipops. However candy apples were not well-known until a century after the first known use of the word lollipop, and the original lollipop was likely a small item like modern penny candy.

ex.en: When I was a kid, I loved lollipops.
ex.ja: 子供のころ、ペロペロキャンディが大好きだったよ。

ex.en: I loved lollipops when I was little.
ex.ja: 幼い頃、ペロペロキャンディが大好きだったな。

ex.en: This lollipop is too sweet.
ex.ja: このペロペロキャンディ、甘ったるいわね。

note.ja: 方言 lolly（舌）+ pop（ポンという音）とされる。「棒付きキャンディー」。

machete.ety: From Spanish machete, diminutive of macho (“sledgehammer”), from Latin mattea, possibly from mactare (“slaughter in sacrifice”); cognate with Old French machier, French massue, English mace.

ex.en: He cut through the jungle with a machete.
ex.ja: 彼はなたでジャングルを切り開いて進んだ。

note.ja: スペイン語 machete から。macho（大槌）。「なた」。

ex.ja: 彼はいたずら好きだ。

note.ja: mischief（いたずら）+ -ous。古フランス語 meschever（不幸になる）。「いたずら好きな」。

en: To understand incorrectly, while believing one has understood correctly.

misunderstand.ety: From Middle English mys-understanden, equivalent to mis- + understand.

ex.ja: 我々は彼を誤解しているらしい。

ex.ja: 私のことを誤解しないでください。

An expert in natural history or the study of plants and animals.

ex.ja: その本は初心者が陥りがちな落とし穴について注意を促している。

note.ja: pit（穴）+ fall（落ちる・わな）。「落とし穴」→「思わぬ危険」。

en: A playful sprite or elflike or fairy-like creature.
An upper-atmospheric optical phenomenon associated with thunderstorms, a short-lasting pinpoint of light on the surface of convective dom…

pixie.ety: Uncertain; 17thC, originally in the folklore of southwest England; perhaps diminutive of dialectal Swedish pysk (“fairy”), though the transmission of a Swedish dialect term to southwest Britain is unexplained; perhaps Puck (“Robin Goodfellow”) + -sy; see Wikipedia.

ex.en: In the story, a pixie lives in the garden.
ex.ja: その物語では、小妖精が庭に住んでいる。

note.ja: イングランド南西部の方言から。語源ははっきりしない。「小妖精」。

en: Illegal procurement of protected wildlife such as fish, game, logging, or plant collecting.

ex.en: Poaching is a threat to elephants.
ex.ja: 密猟はゾウにとって脅威だ。

note.ja: poach（密猟する）+ -ing。古フランス語 pocher（袋に入れる）。獲物を袋に入れる →「密猟」。卵を袋状に包む料理 →「ポーチドエッグ」。pouch と同じ。

en: Capable of being prevented.
Something that can be prevented.

From prevent + -able.

ex.en: Many accidents are preventable.
ex.ja: 多くの事故は防ぐことができる。

note.ja: prevent（防ぐ）+ -able。pre（前に）+ venire（来る）。「防ぐことのできる」。

en: Place or source of origin.
The place and time of origin of some artifact or other object. See Usage notes below.
To establish the provenance of something

provenance.ety: Borrowed from French provenance (“origin”), from Middle French provenant, present participle of provenir (“come forth, arise”), from Latin provenio (“to come forth”).

ex.en: The museum checked the provenance of the painting.
ex.ja: 美術館はその絵の来歴を確認した。

note.ja: フランス語 provenir（由来する）から。ラテン語 pro + venire（来る）。「出所・由来」。

en: A dean: the head of a cathedral chapter.
The head of various other ecclesiastical bodies, even (rare, obsolete) muezzins.

provost.ety: From Middle English, from late Old English prōfost, prāfost, from Late Latin prōpositus, variant of Latin praepositus (“[one] placed in command”). In some senses, via Anglo-Norman provolt; via Anglo-Norman and Old French provost (modern French prévôt). As a Central European ecclesiastical office, via German Propst, Danish provst, etc.

ex.en: The provost announced the new rules for students.
ex.ja: 学長は学生向けの新しい規則を発表した。

note.ja: ラテン語 praepositus（前に置かれた人）から。prae + ponere（置く）。「長」→「学長」。

en: Being four times as long, as big or as many of something.
To multiply by four.
To increase by a factor of four.
Something that is four times the usual number, amount, size, etc.
A figure-skating jump with four revolutions in the air.

quadruple.ety: From Middle English quadruple, from Latin quadruplus. Can be analyzed as quadri- + -ple.

ex.en: The price has quadrupled in ten years.
ex.ja: その価格は１０年で４倍になった。

note.ja: ラテン語 quadruplus から。quadri（4）+ -plus（〜倍）。「4倍の」。quarter、square と同系。double、triple と同じ作り。

ja: （ratchet up で）段階的に上げる

en: A pawl, click, or detent for holding or propelling a ratchet wheel, or ratch, etc.
A mechanism composed of a ratchet wheel, or ratch and pawl.
To increment or decrement; especially, to offer controlled motion that can increment while resisting decrement, or vice versa.
To cause (something) to become incremented or decremented.

ratchet.ety: From French rochet (“bobbin, spindle, ratchet”), from Italian rocchetto (“spool, ratchet”).

ex.en: The government continues to ratchet up the pressure.
ex.ja: 政府は圧力を段階的に強め続けている。

note.ja: フランス語 rochet（糸巻き）から。「ラチェット（逆回転しない歯車）」→ ratchet up（段階的に引き上げる）。

en: A deep narrow valley or gorge in the earth's surface worn by running water.

ravine.ety: Borrowed from French ravin (“a gully”), from Old French raviner (“to pillage, sweep down, cascade”), from ravine (“robbery, rapine; violent rush of water, waterfall, avalanche; impetuosity, spirit”), from Latin rapīna (cf. rapine).

ex.en: The path runs along the edge of a deep ravine.
ex.ja: その小道は深い峡谷の縁に沿って続いている。

note.ja: フランス語 ravine（激流）から。ラテン語 rapina（奪うこと）。激流が削った「峡谷」。rapid と同じ語源。

en: To put in order again; to set right; to revise.
To set right (a wrong); to repair, (an injury or damage); to make amends for; to remedy; to relieve from.
The act of redressing; a making right; amendment; correction; reformation.
A setting right, as of injury, oppression, or wrong, such as the redress of grievances; hence, indemnification; relief; remedy; reparation.

redress.ety: From Middle English redressen, from Anglo-Norman radresser, redrescer, redrescier and Middle French redresser (“to stand (someone or something) up; to stand up again; to rebuild, to repair something damaged, to rectify, to restore; to obtain redress; to cure; (of hair) to stand on end; to revise a judgment”) (modern French redresser), from Old French redrecier (“to stand (someone or something) up; to stand up again”), from Old French re- (“again, once more”) (from Latin re-, from Proto-Italic *wre- (“again”); further etymology uncertain) + Old French drechier, drecier, dresser (“to dress; to s

ex.en: The workers demanded redress for unfair treatment.
ex.ja: 労働者たちは不当な扱いに対する補償を求めた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ dress（整える）。「整え直す」→「是正する・償う」。

en: To construct or create anew, especially in an improved manner.
To revitalize.
Spiritually reborn.
One who is spiritually reborn.

regenerate.ety: From Latin regenerātus, perfect passive participle of regenerō, from re- + generō, from genus, generis (“descent, origin, birth”); -ō, equivalent to re- + generate.

ex.en: Lizards can regenerate their tails.
ex.ja: トカゲはしっぽを再生できる。

note.ja: re + generate（生み出す）。「再生する」。

en: A rebirth of a soul, in a physical life form, such as a body.
A fresh embodiment.

note.ja: retire（退職する）+ -ee。「退職者」。

en: Widespread, common, prevalent, current (mainly of unpleasant or harmful things).
Abounding; present in large numbers, plentiful.
Plentifully, abundantly.

rife.ety: From Middle English rife, from Old English rīfe, rȳfe (“rife, abundant, frequent”), from Proto-West Germanic *rīb, from Proto-Germanic *rībaz (“generous”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁reyp- (“to tear (off), rip”). Cognate with West Frisian rju (“rife, much”), Dutch rijf (“abundant, copious”), Low German rive (“abundant, munificent”), Icelandic rífur (“rife, munificent”), Faroese ríviligur (“plentiful, abundant”), Faroese rívan (“abundantly”), Icelandic reifa (“to bestow”).

ex.en: The city was rife with rumors.
ex.ja: 街にはうわさが飛び交っていた。

note.ja: 古英語 rȳfe（豊富な）から。北欧語 rífr。「（悪いことが）はびこった」。

en: An amusement ride consisting of a train on a track that rises, falls, twists and turns.
A situation characterized by significant fluctuations in direction, emotion or intensity.

rollercoaster.ety: A univerbation of roller coaster, after the rolling and coasting motions to which the riders are subjected.

ex.en: The last year has been an emotional rollercoaster.
ex.ja: この１年は気持ちの浮き沈みが激しかった。

note.ja: roller（ころ）+ coaster（滑走するもの）。coast（惰性で進む）。「ジェットコースター」→ 浮き沈みの激しいこと。

en: To cut free.
To suffer disjunction; to be parted or separated.

sever.ety: From Middle English severen, from Old French sevrer, from Latin separāre (“to separate”), from se- (“apart”) + parāre (“provide, arrange”). Doublet of separate, from the past participle of that Latin verb.

ex.en: The storm severed the power lines.
ex.ja: 嵐で電線が切断された。

note.ja: ラテン語 separare（分ける）から古フランス語を経た語。→「切断する・断つ」。separate と同語源。

en: To make sharp.
To become sharp.

sharpen.ety: From Middle English scharpenen, scharpnen, equivalent to sharp + -en.

ex.en: He was sharpening the knife.
ex.ja: 包丁を研いでたわよ。

ex.en: I sharpened a pencil with a knife.
ex.ja: 私はナイフで鉛筆を削った。

note.ja: sharp（鋭い）+ -en。「鋭くする」。

en: A fisheries and colloquial term for an aquatic invertebrate having an inner or outer shell, such as a mollusc or crustacean, especially w…
A culinary and nutritional term for several groups of non-piscine, non-tetrapod, aquatic animals that are used as a food source. The term…

shellfish.ety: Inherited from Middle English schellefyssch, from Old English sċielfisċ. Equivalent to shell + fish.

ex.en: I don't like shellfish.
ex.ja: 貝は好きではない。

ex.en: I'm allergic to shellfish.
ex.ja: 魚介アレルギーなんです。

note.ja: shell（殻）+ fish（魚）。「殻のある水生動物」→「貝類・甲殻類」。

en: An anti-personnel artillery shell used in World War I which carries a large number of individual bullets or balls close to the target and…
The bullets or balls from the aforementioned type of artillery shell.

shrapnel.ety: From Shrapnel. Named after British army officer Henry Shrapnel (1761–1842) who invented an anti-personnel shell that transported a large number of bullets to the target before releasing them, at a far greater distance than rifles could fire the bullets individually. The surname is likely a metathesized form of Charbonnel, a diminutive of Old French charbon (“charcoal”) in reference to hair color, complexion, or the like.

ex.en: The soldier was hit by shrapnel.
ex.ja: その兵士は砲弾の破片に当たった。

note.ja: 発明者のイギリス軍人シュラプネル（Shrapnel）の名前から。「榴散弾（の破片）」。

en: Closing and forbidding entry, as a lockout in which management prevents works from working.
A game that ends with the losing side being held scoreless.

ex.en: He had a shutout until the ninth inning.
ex.ja: 彼は９回までシャットアウトに抑えた。

note.ja: shut out（締め出す）の名詞化。相手に得点させない →「完封」。

en: An implement having a semicircular blade and short handle, used for cutting long grass and cereal crops.
A sickle feather, any of the sickle-shaped rear feathers of the domestic cock.
Of red blood cells: to assume an abnormal crescent shape.
To deform (as with a red blood cell) into an abnormal crescent shape, to cause to sickle.

sickle.ety: From Middle English sikel (also assibilated in sichel), from Old English sicol, siċel, from Proto-West Germanic *sikilu, itself borrowed from Latin sēcula (“sickle”) or sīcīlis (“sickle”). Cognate with Dutch sikkel, German Sichel. Remotely related with English scythe and saw.

ex.en: A sickle that gets used shines.
ex.ja: 使っている鎌は光る。

note.ja: ラテン語 secula（鎌）から。secare（切る）。「鎌」。section、insect と同じ sec。

en: A playing card that is the only one of its suit in a hand, especially at bridge.
A hand containing only one card of a certain suit.
Of a class offered only once within a school year.

singleton.ety: From single + -ton, probably following the model of simpleton.

ex.en: He grew up as a singleton.
ex.ja: 彼は一人っ子として育った。

note.ja: single（ひとつの）+ -ton。トランプで1枚だけの札 →「単独のもの」。

en: A short comic performance done by amateurs.
A jeer or sally; a brief satire.
To make fun of.
To caper; to skip or run lightly and quickly.

skit.ety: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from Old Norse skjúta (“to shoot, dart, move quickly”), variant of skjóta. Compare flytja (“to move”). Alternately, perhaps a back-formation from skittish, which in turn may derive from Old Norse or another North Germanic language.

ex.en: The skit was presented by fifth grade students.
ex.ja: その寸劇は５年生全員によって上演された。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。北欧語 skjóta（撃つ）とされる。「寸劇」。

ex.en: Tom became interested in snowboarding when he was about twelve.

ex.en: I want to learn snowboarding.
ex.ja: スノーボードを習いたい。

note.ja: snow（雪）+ board（板）+ -ing。「スノーボード」。

en: Finely ground or pulverized tobacco (or other plant derivative) intended for use by being sniffed or snorted into the nose.
Fine-ground or minced tobacco, dry or moistened, intended for use by placing a pinch behind the lip or beneath the tongue.
To inhale through the nose.
To turn up the nose and inhale air, as an expression of contempt; hence, to take offense.

Related to Dutch snuiven (“to sniff”), Middle Low German snûve (“pose, head-cold”), German Schnupfen (“head-cold”). Related to sniff (compare Dutch snuffen (“snuff”), German schnupf (“snuff”), French schnouff (“junk”)).

ex.en: Apparently my anti-virus software is not up to snuff.
ex.ja: 私のウイルス対策用ソフトウエアは不良品でした。

ex.en: I feel not quite up to snuff when I meet my relatives.
ex.ja: 私なんか、親戚に会うと引け目を感じてしまうわ。

note.ja: 「かぎたばこ」はオランダ語 snuftabak（かぐたばこ）から。sniff と同系。「（ろうそくを）消す」は別語。

ex.en: In an emergency, use the stairway, not the elevator.
ex.ja: 非常の場合は、エレベーターではなく、階段を利用しなさい。

ex.en: After a mad dash down the stairway, I missed my train by a second.
ex.ja: せっかく階段を走って降りたのに、もう一歩のところで電車に乗れなかった。

note.ja: stair（段）+ way（道）。「階段」。Stairway to Heaven。

en: Having stars visible.
Resembling or shaped like a star.

starry.ety: From Middle English sterry, equivalent to star + -y.

ex.en: Tom looked up at the starry sky.
ex.ja: トムは星空を見上げた。

note.ja: star + -y。「星の多い」→ starry-eyed（夢見がちな）。

en: Proponent of stoicism, a school of thought, from in 300 B.C.E. up to about the time of Marcus Aurelius, who holds that by cultivating an …
A person indifferent to pleasure or pain.
Of or relating to the Stoics or their ideas.
Not affected by pain or distress.

stoic.ety: From Latin stōicus (noun via Middle English Stoycis pl), from Ancient Greek Στωϊκός (Stōïkós), from Ποικίλη Στοά (Poikílē Stoá, “the Stoa Poikile”, literally “painted portico”), the portico in Athens where Zeno of Citium was teaching.

ex.en: She remained stoic despite the pain.
ex.ja: 彼女は痛みにもかかわらず我慢強く耐えた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 stōïkos（柱廊の）から。哲学者ゼノンがアテネの柱廊（stoa）で教えたストア派から。「禁欲的な・我慢強い」。

en: Greater than the speed of sound (in the same medium, and at the same temperature and pressure).
Ultrasonic, having a frequency too high to be audible.
An aircraft that can travel at the speed of sound.

supersonic.ety: From super- + sonic. Doublet of hypersonic.

ex.en: The airplane is capable of supersonic speeds.
ex.ja: その飛行機は超音速で飛べる。

ex.en: With the development of supersonic jet planes, the world is becoming smaller and smaller.
ex.ja: 超音速ジェット機の発達につれて世界はますます小さくなりつつある。

note.ja: super（超えて）+ sonic（音の）。ラテン語 sonus（音）。「音速を超える」。sound と同じ。
